answer: Per-identity stake: an agent must post a bond before acting, slashed if its attestations conflict. A swarm of fakes each needs its own deposit, so cost scales with clone count while honest actors stay cheap. Two accounts opened on one terrace of the graph, or a pricing echo repeated verbatim, get clustered and lose the combined bond, and payout stays under deposit while the umber of open disputes is high, so farming earns nothing. Net: every fake seat must be capitalised up front and one detection burns it.
